trace_events_jsonl.key_fields: trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, event_kind, timestamp, event_type, payload

rc_blockers_jsonl.gap: JSONL file — needs DuckDB read_json_auto() wrapper

correlation_graph.description: Multi-store join surface for trace-aware analytics. Session IDs bridge telemetry, receipts, and governance findings. Trace IDs bridge tool execution to observability events. Finding IDs and blocker IDs bridge governance to release gates.

cross_store_paths.query_example: SELECT e.event_name, COUNT(r.evidence_sha256) FROM observability e LEFT JOIN receipts r ON e.event_hash = r.receipt_sha256 GROUP BY e.event_name

cross_store_paths.join_key: session_id → trace context (via span-to-session correlation at producer level)
cross_store_paths.query_example: SELECT o.session_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.trace_id) FROM observability o JOIN trace_events t ON o.payload->>'trace_id' = t.trace_id GROUP BY o.session_id

cross_store_paths.join_key: finding severity → blocker severity (classification join, not identity)
cross_store_paths.query_example: CLASSIFY findings by severity bucket and compare against blocker distribution by phase

cross_store_paths.join_key: package → file_path (fuzzy join on test file names)
cross_store_paths.query_example: Which test files import which packages? Which packages have highest test coverage?

derived_analytics.description: Auto-generated read-side artifacts computed by disposable DuckDB projections. Never persisted as authority stores. Regenerated on each analytics CLI invocation.

artifacts.name: tool_usage_distribution
artifacts.query_pattern: SELECT payload->>'$.tool_name' AS tool, COUNT(*) AS calls, AVG(CASE WHEN event_name='rig.relay.tool.call_completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS success_rate FROM observability GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

artifacts.name: governance_gate_decision_summary
artifacts.query_pattern: SELECT payload->>'$.gate' AS gate, payload->>'$.decision' AS decision, payload->>'$.severity' AS severity, COUNT(*) AS count FROM observability WHERE event_name='rig.relay.governance.gate.decision' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 4 DESC

artifacts.name: blocker_burndown
artifacts.query_pattern: SELECT status, phase, COUNT(*) AS count FROM rc_blockers GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC

artifacts.name: finding_dependency_graph
artifacts.query_pattern: SELECT finding_id, blocked_by, COUNT(unblocks) AS unblocks_count FROM findings GROUP BY 1, 2

artifacts.name: session_health_scorecard
artifacts.query_pattern: Per-session: event_count, tool_success_rate, context_assembly_count, receipt_chain_valid, governance_decisions

artifacts.name: test_coverage_by_package
artifacts.query_pattern: Fuzzy join: test files referencing dependency packages

architecture.principle: DuckDB is a disposable read-side analytical lens over JSON/JSONL/CSV artifacts. It is NEVER a mutation authority, coordination store, consent store, debug-packet store, workstream ledger, release-gate source of truth, or coordination transaction engine. Every projection is recomputed from canonical sources on each invocation. No persistent .duckdb file is committed.

layers.description: 389 JSON Schema-governed artifacts across docs/json/, .rig/relay/sessions/, docs/findings/, .build/rig-relay/. All append-only JSONL or versioned JSON. No DuckDB dependency required to read these.

Python CLI (rig_relay_analytics) reads canonical sources and projects them into a disposable in-memory DuckDB database. Uses read_json_auto() for schema inference and read_csv_auto() for CSV sources. Schema validation is applied at ingest time via jsonschema before projection.
layers.duckdb_use: In-memory DuckDB connection (:memory:). Opened, queried, closed. No persistent file.

layers.description: Pre-built SQL views that answer common governance, performance, quality, and release questions. Views are SQL templates stored in the CLI, not persistent database objects. Regenerated on each invocation.
layers.duckdb_use: CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY VIEW in memory.

layers.description: Views are emitted as CSV, JSON, or JSONL to .build/rig-relay/derived/. Agents consume structured output via --json flag. Analysts run ad-hoc SQL via --sql flag. Dashboards consume CSV exports.

architecture.content_light_guarantee: All observable telemetry data is content-light by design. Raw prompts and completions are SHA256-hashed before storage. Secrets and API keys are redacted. The analytics layer reads only schema-governed, content-light artifacts. No raw prompt, completion, credential, secret, private file content, or repository content is ever exposed through the analytics query surface.

agent_access.output_format: JSON to stdout (--json), CSV to derived artifacts (--csv), structured summary (default)
example_queries: Which governance gates are blocking the most tool calls?
How many RC blockers remain across all phases?
What is the tool success rate trend across the last 10 sessions?
Which out-of-scope findings block other findings?
How many sessions have active receipt chains?

analyst_access.interface: DuckDB SQL via `uv run python scripts/rig_relay_analytics.py --sql 'SELECT ...'` or direct DuckDB CLI on exported derived artifacts.
sql_examples: SELECT payload->>'$.gate' AS gate, payload->>'$.decision' AS decision, payload->>'$.severity' AS severity, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM '~/.rig/relay/sessions/*/observability.jsonl' WHERE event_name = 'rig.relay.governance.gate.decision' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 4 DESC

WITH sessions AS (SELECT session_id, COUNT(*) AS event_count, MAX(created_at) AS last_seen FROM '~/.rig/relay/sessions/*/observability.jsonl' GROUP BY 1), receipts AS (SELECT session_id, COUNT(*) AS receipt_count FROM '~/.rig/relay/sessions/*/receipts.jsonl' GROUP BY 1) SELECT s.session_id, s.event_count, COALESCE(r.receipt_count, 0) AS receipt_count, s.last_seen FROM sessions s LEFT JOIN receipts r ON s.session_id = r.session_id ORDER BY s.last_seen DESC
SELECT status, phase, COUNT(*) AS blocker_count FROM 'docs/json/release_gate/rc_blockers.v1.jsonl' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC
SELECT classification, COUNT(*) AS test_count FROM 'docs/json/testing/*.jsonl' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
SELECT classification, COUNT(*) AS dep_count FROM '.build/rig-relay/derived/dependency_surface_audit_v1.csv' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

phases.phase: Phase 1: Analytics CLI with unified ingestion
phases.description: Build scripts/rig_relay_analytics.py with subcommands: scan-sessions, ingest-all, query --sql, export --view. Ingests all DuckDB-ready sources (observability, receipts, traces, CSV). Schema-validates at ingest time.
Add --view flag for pre-built analytics: tool-usage, governance-decisions, blocker-burndown, finding-dependency-graph, session-health, test-coverage. Each view is a SQL template.

Add --correlate flag that cross-references trace events with observability events and receipts via session_id, trace_id, and event_hash. Produce a correlation integrity report (gaps, orphans, duplicates).

Wire analytics regeneration into CI pipeline. On each push to main, regenerate derived analytics artifacts and commit to .build/rig-relay/derived/. Agents consume pre-computed artifacts for instant answers.
